surfaces.part: flat sedum roof with parapet and skylight

answer.evidence: Rows 0-39 show the roof seen from above. A grey parapet frames a green sedum bed (rows 11-33) with a skylight panel in the middle, and the light parapet front edge sits near rows 36-38. This is contents visible inside an open frame (evidence d). Below it the cornice (rows ~41-47) and a tall south facade (rows ~48-143) carry windows, balconies and a door canopy. That gives about 100 rows of front face. No receding side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's measured facts sit within the reference range. It has 15 colours per tile against 18 and 11 for the references, and 53 distinct colours against 66 for the stone reference (the other reference has 185). Flat-fill coverage is 4%, and 0% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines lean visibly toward the material (purple-grey stone frame, dark blue-grey window frames, dark green around the foliage) rather than being a black sticker line. The sedum roof is the strongest part: it has clumped foliage in about 4-5 greens, with reddish dots and per-clump highlights and shadows. The cream wall has a speckle texture, and the balconies have railing detail, pink curtains and lit window panes. The weaker points are that the wall ramp is only about 3-4 steps against the 5-6 of the tile roofs and plaster, and that the facade repeats the same window pattern. Even so, it would sit next to the references without looking flat or sticker-like, so it is slightly lower in density but acceptable.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a whole building (roof garden, walls, windows, door), so it matches the reference kind. Measured facts: 15 colours per tile against 18 and 11 for the references, so it is above the stone reference and close to h101. Flat-fill coverage is 4%, which is low and has no large dead areas. 0% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines carry a tint. In the image the window frames and the gray parapet edge lean blue-gray, and the foliage edges lean dark green, rather than being a uniform black line. The sedum roof has several greens with red-brown accents and reads as clumped foliage. The cream walls have speckle dots plus a shaded balcony band and trim.
